claim: api.fda.gov/device/udi.json returns full GUDID records without an API key under CC0 (except GMDN/DUNS), with fields identifiers[].id, sterilization, is_single_use, has_lot_or_batch_number, has_expiration_date, premarket_submissions; limits 240/min and 1,000/day keyless, 120,000/day with a free key.
evidence: Live keyless curl on 2026-10-18 of https://api.fda.gov/device/udi.json?search=brand_name:stent&limit=1 returned HTTP 200 (meta.last_updated 2026-10-01, total 7,385 matching records, Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *). The returned record (RelayPro NBS Thoracic Stent-Graft System, Bolton Medical) contains every field named in the claim: identifiers[0].id = "00843576164437" (type Primary, issuing_agency GS1), sterilization {is_sterile, is_sterilization_prior_use}, is_single_use, has_lot_or_batch_number, has_expiration_date, premarket_submissions [{submission_number P200045, supplement_number 002}], plus brand_name, version_or_model_number, catalog_number, product_codes with openfda annotation (device_class), gmdn_terms, device_sizes, storage, mri_safety, labeler_duns_number and company_name. Response meta links to terms (open.fda.gov/terms) and license (open.fda.gov/license). open.fda.gov/apis/authentication states exactly: without key 240 requests/min per IP and 1,000 requests/day per IP; with key 240/min per key and 120,000/day per key (key is free). open.fda.gov/license and /terms state content is public domain under CC0 1.0 "unless otherwise noted", with an explicit exception that GMDN Term Code/Name/Definition is licensed from The GMDN Agency and extraction for commercial services or AI training requires a licence. The DUNS exception is not on openFDA's licence page; it comes from the AccessGUDID (NLM) terms page (accessgudid.nlm.nih.gov/terms), which says D&B data is provided for FDA internal use only, is proprietary to D&B, and may not be used commercially or further disclosed. The openFDA UDI endpoint page says data is refreshed weekly (observed last_updated 2026-10-01). No rate-limit headers are returned on a single request, so the limits were verified from docs, not by load testing.
correction: Claim is accurate. Minor precision: the keyless limits are per IP address (240/min, 1,000/day) and keyed limits are per key (240/min, 120,000/day), so the per-minute cap does not rise with a key. The GMDN carve-out is stated by openFDA itself; the DUNS carve-out is stated in the AccessGUDID/NLM terms (D&B data for FDA internal use only, no commercial use or redistribution), not on openFDA's licence page, but the same labeler_duns_number field is present in openFDA records, so treat it as restricted. Data is refreshed weekly, not real-time.
impact_on_candidate: No negative impact; the data plan stands. The free, keyless endpoint provides every structured field needed for a synthetic label benchmark and a UDI-DI consistency check (GTIN/UDI-DI, sterility, single-use, lot/expiry flags, PMA/510(k) numbers, product codes, device class, sizes, storage conditions). Practical cautions for the build: (1) strip or do not redistribute gmdn_terms and labeler_duns_number in any published benchmark or demo dataset to stay inside the GMDN and D&B restrictions; (2) register a free API key before bulk pulls, since 1,000/day keyless is tight for building a benchmark of thousands of records (or use the bulk JSON download files from open.fda.gov/data/downloads to avoid rate limits entirely); (3) openFDA warns results are unvalidated and should not be used for medical-care decisions, so position the data as a demo/benchmark source, not a regulatory source of truth.
